articles.title: Texans GM Nick Caserio gives high praise to rookie OL Keylan Rutledge
articles.summary: Houston Texans general manager had several quotes that certainly caught the attention of the public following Tuesday's roster cutdown, but his comments on K...
articles.body:
Houston Texans general manager had several quotes that certainly caught the attention of the public following Tuesday's roster cutdown.

But even with comments surrounding the contract negotiations with quarterback C.J. Stroud, Caserio might have opened the public to rookie Keylan Rutledge, a player he's sold on being perhaps the top option on the offensive line entering Week 1's matchup against the Buffalo Bills .

"Honestly, he's probably the best offensive lineman that we have," Caserio said. "We're glad he's here."

A first-round pick out of Georgia Tech, Rutledge was brought into Houston to compete for the starting job. It was a transition role, especially given that he never played the position before following his time at guard with both the Yellow Jackets and at Middle Tennessee State.

So far in camp, Rutledge has been fine at center, but he's thrived when asked to play left guard. In both preseason matchups, he started next to Evan Brown on the left side and excelled in run-blocking sets. Meanwhile, Brown has been servicable as a center and likely will take snaps Week 1 against Buffalo.

"At some point, we're going to say in the end, we feel this is probably the best spot for that player, understanding that those reps that they get at the other position could potentially come into play at some point down the road," Caserio said. "In the end we feel like Keylan right now is the best left guard."

But for Caserio to call Rutledge the team's best offensive lineman, featuring multiple players with Pro Bowl potential, is a high compliment for someone who's yet to take a professional snap. It could prevail and become a reason to believe Houston's offensive line has turned the corner, but say the rookie struggles against Titans All-Pro Jeffery Simmons or newly-signed Dexter Lawrence from Cincinnati?

What does that say about the rest of the line in general?

images.caption: Texans GM Nick Caserio gives high praise to rookie OL Keylan Rutledge

articles.title: Houston Astros' Carlos Correa cleared for important next step in rehab, but hurdles still remain
articles.summary: Carlos Correa, who says he's sprinting at "95%," will ramp up his baseball activities in Florida in his bid to return to the Astros this season.
articles.body:
Third baseman Carlos Correa was cleared Tuesday to take a significant next step in his attempt to return to the Houston Astros this year from ankle surgery.

Correa, who had surgery in early May for a torn peroneus brevis tendon, had a doctor's appointment Tuesday at which he was cleared to increase his baseball activities. The plan is for Correa to report to the Astros ' minor-league facility in West Palm Beach, Fla., this weekend to begin that ramp-up.

"From the moment I had the surgery, my plan has always been to try to get back and play this year," Correa said Tuesday. "So now that we're going to ramp up for real and see how the foot's going to respond, this will be a real test for us to see if we can come back and play."

Correa has increased his activity over the past month while rehabbing in Houston . He is hitting against a pitching machine, taking ground balls and sprinting at "95%" at this point, he said.

Correa has not run bases or faced live pitching, two significant hurdles that would be part of his program in Florida. He will not be playing in games there immediately, as there are still boxes he must check.

"It's going to be change of direction, it's going to be the bases, touching the bases, it's going to be the sliding part, the diving part," Correa said. "It's going to be adjusting to certain pitches, hitting the brakes on that front foot. So, Florida will tell us a lot."

In Houston, Correa said he has been "moving pretty well" in side-to-side tests and fielding grounders. He estimated he could stay in Florida "probably a week and a half, or a week, and depending on how it goes we're going to move forward." If the work in Florida goes well, Correa said he would still require a minor-league rehab assignment to play in games before possibly returning to the majors.

The Astros entered Tuesday with 24 games left in the regular season, creating the question of whether a return for Correa, whose surgery was initially thought to be season-ending , is viable. The window could expand if the Astros reach the postseason. They entered Tuesday with a two-game lead in the American League West over the Rangers, plus the tiebreaker over Texas .

Correa said "we're weighing all the options" when asked if his returning solely for a potential postseason run is a possibility. Astros manager Joe Espada cautioned against looking too far ahead regarding Correa, but he acknowledged that Correa going to Florida is "a step closer for him to getting back."

"We've still got to make sure that we check all the boxes, (gauge with) the time he spends on his feet and moving around how he bounces back," Espada said. "But this is really encouraging."

A potential return by Correa also creates intrigue in how Houston would adjust. Espada said if Correa can return: "He'll play third base." Correa said he would not return if limited to hitting as: "I don't think I'm a better DH than Yordan" Alvarez.

Correa said he has worked defensively only at third base in his rehab. Houston reinstalled Isaac Paredes as its regular third baseman after Correa's injury, and Paredes has been its third-most productive hitter by OPS-plus after shortstop Jeremy Peña and Alvarez.

Keeping Paredes in the lineup would remain a priority if Correa returns. Paredes has played at both first base, where Christian Walker is stationed, and second base, where Jose Altuve has played exclusively in the field this season. Espada said he has not "gotten that far" regarding possible roster adjustments.

images.caption: Carlos Correa, who says he's sprinting at "95%," will ramp up his baseball activities in Florida in his bid to return to the Astros this season. (Brett Coomer/Houston Chronicle)

articles.title: Ravens to sign former Rams offensive tackle AJ Arcuri to practice squad
articles.summary: Baltimore is adding former Rams offensive lineman AJ Arcuri to its practice squad.
articles.body:
The Baltimore Ravens are adding another developmental option to their offensive line entering the regular season.

Baltimore is signing former Los Angeles Rams offensive lineman AJ Arcuri to its practice squad, according to Mike Garafolo of NFL Network. The move gives Arcuri a fresh start after spending the first four years of his professional career with the Rams. Los Angeles selected Arcuri in the seventh round of the 2022 NFL draft out of Michigan State. The 6-foot-7, 320-pound lineman has primarily worked at offensive tackle and provides Baltimore with another experienced option who can develop behind its active roster group.

Arcuri appeared in two regular-season games for the Rams during his first three NFL seasons, including one start. Although his opportunities were limited, he spent multiple years learning within an organization that consistently asked its offensive linemen to execute a varied running game and operate effectively in play-action concepts.

Baltimore's decision to sign Arcuri provides the team with additional insurance at a premium position. Practice-squad linemen are often needed throughout a 17-game regular season as injuries and weekly roster management test a team's depth.

Arcuri also offers the size and length that Ravens offensive line coach Dwayne Ledford can continue to develop. He will have time to learn Baltimore's terminology and blocking system without immediately being forced into the lineup.

The Ravens finalized their initial practice squad earlier in the week, but those units remain fluid throughout the season. Adding Arcuri allows Baltimore to evaluate a young, experienced tackle while giving the former seventh-round pick an opportunity to establish himself in a new organization.

images.caption: Ravens to sign former Rams offensive tackle AJ Arcuri to practice squad

articles.title: CBS has no comment about Tony Romo's statement
articles.summary: On Tuesday, former Cowboys quarterback and CBS broadcaster Tony Romo issued a statement announcing his no-contest plea to OWI charges and expressing his inte...
articles.body:
On Tuesday, former Cowboys quarterback and CBS broadcaster Tony Romo issued a statement announcing his no-contest plea to OWI charges and expressing his intention to return to CBS, in time.

In response, CBS has nothing to say. And all that that implies.

Via John Ourand of Puck , CBS had no comment about the Romo statement. CBS also referred to its prior statement on Romo — a perfunctory, one-line release announcing that he would be placed on leave " until further notice ."

As Ourand observes, the fact that Romo's statement wasn't coordinated with CBS speaks to a wedge between the two sides, along with the possibly inevitable legal wrangling over the four years and $72 million left on his contract.

And, as Ourand reiterates, "it still appears exceedingly unlikely" that Romo will ever return to CBS.

CBS has done nothing to contradict the perception that it's moving on from Romo, after nine years on the network's No. 1 broadcast team. J.J. Watt has been bumped up to the top spot, and by all appearances he'll be given a full and fair chance to retain it beyond 2026.

articles.title: Cowboys’ Brian Schottenheimer Revealed How 4,139-Yard Passer Won QB2 Job
articles.summary: The Dallas Cowboys have drawn a lot of attention since they cut the roster to 53 players, but one position battle ended in a way no one saw coming.Sam Howell...
articles.body:
The Dallas Cowboys have drawn a lot of attention since they cut the roster to 53 players, but one position battle ended in a way no one saw coming.

Sam Howell ended up winning the QB2 job over Joe Milton III in training camp. The team made that obvious by releasing Milton.

There is still talk that the Cowboys want to bring Milton back to the practice squad, but it would have to be his choice. Many outside of the organization, though, are still wondering how Howell won the job over Milton.

Dallas Cowboys HC Brian Schottenheimer on Sam Howell as QB2

Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer dove into the reason why the team chose Howell over Milton for the starting job. It wasn't just the preseason that decided it for Schottenheimer.

"When we looked at the whole body of work we felt like Sam had done a little bit better of executing the offense."

Howell's preseason performance certainly helped his case for the starting job. He completed 67.5% of his passes for 314 yards and 3 touchdowns to 1 interception in three games. Howell also ran 4 times for 24 yards.

Sam Howell Wins Cowboys' QB2 Job Over Joe Milton

Throughout training camp and preseason, it appeared it was a close battle between Howell and Milton. Both guys were wheeling and dealing throughout the preseason. It's why the offense looked so good in all three games.

To Howell's credit, he's got more experience in the NFL than Milton does. His time with teams like the Washington Commanders , Minnesota Vikings , Seattle Seahawks , and Philadelphia Eagles helped him be the QB he is today.

Howell has developed the right approach while gaining experience on the field. It hasn't always been smooth for him, but it's been good for him.

His maturity in handling the quarterback situation seemed to have impressed the Cowboys. It was enough for them to believe that he's the right man to back up Dak Prescott rolling into the 2026 season.

The hope is that Howell never sees the field unless it is a blowout win or the Cowboys are kneeling the ball down to win. Still, with Prescott's tendency to get hurt, it's good to know they have Howell to trust in games.

Nothing has happened with Milton yet, and he may be looking for other options as a backup or starter elsewhere. If he comes back to Dallas, that would be a game changer for the Cowboys and only make them better at QB. For now, Howell is the man responsible for easing Cowboys fans' minds as Prescott's backup.

articles.title: Husker Volleyball Travels to Bergen’s Home State to Play South Dakota State
articles.summary: South Dakota State2025 Record: 23-52025 Conference Record: The Summit League (16-0)Last NCAA Tournament Appearance: 2025 (Lost to Arizona in 1st Round) After...
articles.body:
South Dakota State 2025 Record: 23-5 2025 Conference Record: The Summit League (16-0) Last NCAA Tournament Appearance: 2025 (Lost to Arizona in 1st Round)

After an exciting first weekend of volleyball, the Huskers will get to play a more lowkey matchup as they head to the home state of Bergen Reilly to play South Dakota State on Wednesday night. These two teams met just last year in the Huskers' annual spring match in the town of Ord, Nebraska.

This match will be one of the Huskers last matches before they finally get to play at the Bob Devaney Center for the first time this season. After their trip to South Dakota, they will head to Chicago to play DePaul on their home court then the much anticipated match against Missouri at Wrigley Field.

South Dakota State has been one of the best teams in the Summit League for the past few years as they have won the Regular Season title two years in a row (2024-2025). They haven't been as successful in the postseason tournament though. They haven't won it since 2007 and finished as the runner-up in 2024 and 2025.

The Jackrabbits are currently 1-2 right now beating Sacramento State, in 5 sets, in their 1st match and then got swept by Pepperdine and lost in 5 to Villanova, who is receiving votes. They are favored to win the Summit League again while the team who beat them in the conference championship, the St. Thomas Tommies, are right behind them tied for 2nd with the South Dakota Coyotes.

SDSU placed 2 girls on the Players to Watch list put out by the conference this year. Both are seniors on the team and both have been at SDSU since they came in as freshman.

DS/L Joslyn Richardson and OH Sylvie Zgonc came into the program in a year where they finished 9-20 overall and lost in the 1st round of the conference tournament. By the next season, everything had turned around and the team went 27-3 overall. Since then, they haven't looked back and these two seniors have been a big part of the turn around.

Senior OH Sylvie Zgonc played in 29 matches in her freshman year, 2023, earning her a spot on the Summit League First Team and was also named Freshman of the Year for the league. In 2024, she won Summit League Player of the Year and then repeated this a year later in 2025. She also has received several AVCA awards throughout the years as well.

The team has lost some fire power on their offense, losing Annalee Ventling-Brown and Sydni Schetnan to graduation, but they have solidified SO OH/RS Hannah Klein as Zgonc's right hand woman. Last season, Klein had 233 kills, 2.24 kills/set, and already has 35 this season in 13 sets played. She has also added 6 blocks as well.

Junior MB Madison Burr and SR MB Brooklyn Meyer have also been big parts of the team's success as well, but they have yet to play this season as it seems like their coach is playing with their lineup in the first few matches. We could possibly see them play Wednesday night.

Instead of Burr and Meyer playing, Freshman MB Hannah Misna has been given a chance early in the season to play and has already recorded 8 blocks in 3 matches, which is 2nd on the team to Claire Logeais' 10 blocks. Logeais is a sophomore transfer from Dayton and has been trying to get herself into the lineup, which will be hard because of the veterans who have proved themselves already.

While SDSU has had a lot of success in the past, the Huskers are coming into town to try and reach 3-0 this season. Beating Nebraska would be a huge win for SDSU, but the Huskers need not look at this match like it is just SDSU. The Jackrabbits are still a good opponent and they could have issues with them if they play down to their level.

Wednesday's match will begin at 7:00pm CST at the First Bank & Trust Arena in Brookings, SD. Sadly, if you are wanting to watch this match, you will need to sign up with MidCo Sports Plus to be able to watch which costs $10 to get a Single Game Pass. This should be the only match this season that requires extra payment to watch, besides matches on B1G+, but we are used to those. articles.title: Toronto Blue Jays Release High-Risk 20-Year-Old During Guardians Series
articles.summary: The Toronto Blue Jays released a high-risk 20-year-old pitcher during their series against the Cleveland Guardians. The post Toronto Blue Jays Release High-R...
articles.body:
The Toronto Blue Jays are entering one of the most important series of the 2026 season against the Cleveland Guardians. At the same time, the Blue Jays have announced news regarding Edgar Gallegos.

September is a new month for the Blue Jays, after exiting the best month of their season to date. Game 1 of their series versus the Guardians starts on Tuesday night, with Spencer Miles as the opener going against Gavin Williams of the Guardians.

The game will be broadcast at 6:40 PM Eastern Time, 4:40 PM Mountain Time.

Toronto Blue Jays Release 20-Year-Old Pitcher

The Blue Jays made an announcement regarding Gallegos before the first pitch of the series was thrown.

According to the MiLB Transactions Log, the Blue Jays released Gallegos : "FCL Blue Jays released RHP Edgar Gallegos.

Gallegos is a 20-year-old pitcher . The 6-foot-5, 198-pound hurler was in his third season with the organization.

The Blue Jays originally signed Gallegos to a minor league contract on March 24th, 2024.

He played in the Dominican Summer League for the first two years of his Blue Jays tenure. In 2026, Gallegos played 14 games in the Florida Complex League and one game with the Dunedin Blue Jays.

The numbers suggest he wasn't the strongest pitcher one way or another.

In 14 FCL games, Gallegos recorded 16 strikeouts in 20.2 innings. Sadly, his WHIP (2.08) and ERA (9.15) are inflated by the large volume of hits (36), earned runs (21), and home runs (6) scored off him.

The strikeout numbers aren't substantial enough to elicit excitement. However, not being able to prevent runs from being scored is a big mark against Gallegos' record.

Could the Toronto Blue Jays Bring Back Edgar Gallegos?

In his single appearance for Dunedin, he put up an admirable performance. In the one game, Gallegos recorded two strikeouts while surrendering a single hit in three innings to earn a save.

While he isn't blowing the doors off of the minor leagues with his strikeout numbers or notable velocity, it's promising that he was able to handle a clutch situation.

Could the Blue Jays bring Gallegos back? This could be a situation where the door is not completely closed on a return.

Given how well he performed in the single game, at the very least, he warrants another look.

articles.title: Bengals Pushed to Sign $118 Million Pro Bowl Player After Roster Cuts
articles.summary: Following final roster cuts and waiver wire transactions, we now have a pretty good idea of how the Cincinnati Bengals will look heading into the 2026 season...
articles.body:
Following final roster cuts and waiver wire transactions, we now have a pretty good idea of how the Cincinnati Bengals will look heading into the 2026 season.

Excitement is high around the Bengals. After three consecutive seasons of missing the postseason, the Bengals' front office spent aggressively in free agency and pulled off a blockbuster trade for three-time Pro Bowl defensive lineman Dexter Lawrence.

Last season, Cincinnati struggled heavily on defense, and while the expectation is that these moves will massively improve their defense, there are still areas where the team could get better before Week 1. As a result, the team has been pushed to sign a 10-time Pro Bowl linebacker.

Cincinnati Bengals Pushed to Sign Bobby Wagner

StripeHype's Brandon Johnson listed three players the Cincinnati Bengals should target before their regular season opener. Among those players was future Hall-of-Fame linebacker Bobby Wagner.

Johnson wrote: "Cincinnati clearly believes in its young linebackers, and that confidence may prove justified. But there's a difference between trusting Knight and Carter to play significant roles and entering a championship-or-bust season with almost no margin for error behind them…

Signing Wagner wouldn't require Cincinnati to abandon its youth movement at linebacker. Knight and Carter could remain central pieces of Golden's rebuilt defense while Wagner provides an experienced alternative capable of stepping into a significant role if necessary.

He would also provide insurance against injury at a position where Cincinnati can least afford one.

The Bengals going unusually light at linebacker could indicate they're comfortable supplementing the position with practice-squad elevations and utilizing their considerable depth elsewhere on defense.

Or it could mean the roster isn't finished yet.

Wagner is long in the tooth at 36 years old. Nevertheless, he's productive and available without the Bengals needing to surrender draft capital or win another waiver claim.

For a team that's spent the offseason behaving like its Super Bowl window is right now, this is exactly the type of late-August opportunity it shouldn't ignore."

The Cincinnati Bengals have been linked to Wagner all offseason, and while the team has shown no signs of being interested in the veteran, that could potentially change with Wagner likely being available on a cheap contract.

The reason the team is constantly mentioned as a potential destination for the veteran is that Cincinnati's young linebackers struggled in 2025. And despite the team's belief that they will improve, they are still a question mark on a roster that appears capable of contention.

In May, Sports Illustrated's Gilberto Manzano named the Bengals the best fit for Wagner, as he wrote: "Cincinnati finally made improvements to its poor defense, but spent most of the offseason working on the defensive line, with the trade for Dexter Lawrence II, and the signings of Boye Mafe and Jonathan Allen.

The back end of the defense still needs plenty of help, but all these holes likely won't be fixed in one year. However, it would go a long way if Cincinnati added Wagner to patrol the middle of the field to make sure everything goes smoothly for this new-look front. Yes, Wagner was an issue in coverage for the Commanders last year, but he's still a quality sideline-to-sideline playmaker and his high football IQ would benefit any team."

articles.title: ODU expert warns against heat-related illness for high school athletes
articles.summary: NORFOLK, Va. (WAVY) — Samm Scarneo-Miller says the bright sun and searing heat of late summer can bring dark days for high school athletes. “As soon as July...
articles.body:
NORFOLK, Va. (WAVY) — Samm Scarneo-Miller says the bright sun and searing heat of late summer can bring dark days for high school athletes.

"As soon as July 25 hits, my phone is going to start pinging left and right from friends around the country telling me another kid died," she said in a Tuesday interview.

The assistant professor of athletic training at Old Dominion University consults at sporting events in other regions, and has been an expert witness in cases of heat exertion injury and death.

Scarneo-Miller said team practices this time of year, especially football, are dangerous without the right precautions.

"Going into these triple-digit numbers, we need to be very cognizant of the fact that people are very likely to get exertional heat illnesses with very little effort," she said.

Confusion, altered mental status, slurred speech

Very high body temperature (105+ degrees)

Scarneo-Miller said it's important to know what to do when those signs emerge and an athlete is in jeopardy.

"Exertional heat stroke can be fatal if it is not properly recognized," she said. "However, when it is properly recognized and treated within 30 minutes of collapse, it is 100% survivable. The way that we can save people's lives is by having a tub, water and ice."

Immersion in the ice water bath is what will get the core body temperature below the critical threshold of 105 degrees, and Scarneo-Miller isn't afraid to be creative.

"I have treated patients in a garbage can before — at a cross-country meet, we didn't have enough immersion tubs, and we cleared out a garbage can."

Virginia has restrictions when it comes to two-a-day practices, but Scarneo-Miller said unlike 21 other states, Virginia does not take into account what's known as wet bulb globe temperature.

"It takes into account air temperature, radiation, wind speed and humidity, whereas heat index is only talking about air temp and humidity," she said.

Korey Stringer was a Minnesota Vikings lineman who died of heat-related illness in 2001. The Korey Stringer Institute ranks the states for how well their policies address safety for athletes in in extreme heat. Virginia is among the worst at number 46. North Carolina makes the top 10 at number 8. Georgia was ranked the best.

articles.title: ‘This Is Upsetting,’ ‘Shameful’ — Browns Fans React As Todd Monken Is Unbothered by Backlash Over Deshaun Watson-Shedeur Sanders Decision
articles.summary: The Cleveland Browns have been in quarterback purgatory for many years, and that likely will remain the case as we enter the 2026 season. This offseason, the...
articles.body:
The Cleveland Browns have been in quarterback purgatory for many years, and that likely will remain the case as we enter the 2026 season. This offseason, they had a quarterback competition between Deshaun Watson and Shedeur Sanders.

Neither option stood out this offseason, but the Browns had to start someone, and much to the chagrin of the Cleveland fans, head coach Todd Monken went with Watson. Now, he is shooting down the backlash from his controversial decision.

Todd Monken Not Worried About Disgruntled Browns Fans

It couldn't be clearer that Browns fans don't like Watson and vice versa; however, that didn't affect Monken or his decision.

Monken spoke to the media about his decision to start Watson and whether he let fans' opinions factor into it.

"Absolutely not," he said. "Would I prefer we all be on the same page? Yeah, but that has nothing to do with my decision."

Monken may not be accustomed to the Browns faithful, but he is not gaining himself any brownie points with this decision and subsequent reaction. He made it clear that his job is to do what's best for the football team now and going forward. Browns fans were frustrated by his response.

One fan said, "This is upsetting. [Kevin] Stefanski would always take the fans into consideration. Shameful!"

Maybe one reason Stefanski is no longer with the Browns is that he worried about his perception among fans. Monken is obviously taking a different approach, and we will see how that works out for him.

BE THE GM OF YOUR FAVORITE TEAM: PFN's Free NFL Mock Draft Simulator

Another user said , "Man he better hope Watson plays well." Monken is putting a lot of faith in Watson, who has not played since 2024.

Sanders hasn't shown much when given the chance to play. He struggled last season (ranking No. 37 out of 38 eligible quarterbacks in PFN's QB Impact Score ) and clearly didn't show enough to win the starting job this offseason.

Another fan on X feels fans should be treated better, since they are the ones who pay to support the team. He said, "Yeah, who cares about the fans that pay for tickets…"

While fans play an important role for every NFL team, it doesn't seem like a good idea for an NFL coach to take advice from them. Just because fans want Sanders to start doesn't mean he is necessarily the best option for the team.

Browns fans seem pretty set on making things uncomfortable for their team at home games this season, so don't be surprised if there are plenty of boos.

One fan said, "He better hope and pray they don't come back 0-2 or he'll be bothered then! Good and bothered."

Another added , "Now let's ask Monken how he's gonna handle 60,000 people not only booing but throwing crap at Watson if he plays the home opener."

The Browns have their first two games on the road, then return home in Week 3 in what could be a rocky opener if Watson does not play well the first two weeks.

This is not an ideal start to the season for the Browns, and the games have not even begun yet; the only cure is to win games. However, that doesn't seem likely given this roster.

articles.title: Everton’s Folarin Balogun move collapses as striker walks away from £40m deal
articles.summary: Everton had looked to renegotiate their deal for Balogun but the United States striker then had a change of heart
articles.body:
Everton 's £40m deal with Monaco for Folarin Balogun collapsed after the transfer window shut after the United States striker walked away from the move at the 11th hour.

The Premier League side had reached an agreement to sign the 25-year-old but the forward's medical threw up an issue and Everton looked to renegotiate the agreement.

However, Balogun then decided that he did not want to join Everton after all, leaving David Moyes with only one senior striker after Beto was sold to Fiorentina earlier on deadline day.

Everton explored a late move for Manchester United forward Joshua Zirkzee but their offer of a season-long loan was rejected, leaving Thierno Barry as Everton's only striker.

Monaco needed to sell on deadline day but the collapse of their deal for Balogun will not revive Chelsea's pursuit of midfielder Lamine Camara.

Chelsea are said to be furious after Monaco pulled the plug on a £47m deal for the 22-year-old midfielder after the Blues had sold Enzo Fernandez to Manchester City for £125m.

Everton have ended their long search for a new right-back by signing Ainsley Maitland-Niles from Lyon for around £4.2m.

The former Arsenal player has signed a three-year contract at Hill Dickinson Stadium.

articles.title: 5 major storylines for Penn State heading into 2026 season
articles.summary: Penn State opens up the 2026 season against Marshall on Saturday, so let’s look at the biggest storylines heading into the game.
articles.body:
Almost nothing about Penn State's football team is the same since the last time they took the field back in December. They have a new coach in Matt Campbell , a new starting quarterback in Rocco Becht , and even a new-look Beaver Stadium as we head into 2026.

With so much change taking place at Penn State, there is a lot to unpack about the team's roster, philosophies and outlook for the season. The Nittany Lions have a plethora of questions to answer in both the long-term and short-term, but for now, let's look at the five biggest stories surrounding the team heading into Week 1.

One of the biggest questions of the offseason, and now one of the biggest mysteries of this first game is what Penn State's running back rotation will look like. They have three talented rushers — Carson Hansen , James Peoples , and Quinton Martin Jr. — who all seem capable of handling starter responsibilities.

But with so many mouths to feed, offensive coordinator Taylor Mouser will have his hands full trying to figure out a proper distribution. Will he feed the hot hand from week to week, or will he build a comprehensive plan for the position group that is solidified for the entire season? There is a lot we still don't know about the running back room, but Saturday's game against Marshall should be a good indication of what it will look like going forward.

Senior defensive back Zion Tracy has been relatively quiet in his first three years with the Nittany Lions , but he's expected to have a big role this season. The coaching staff has hinted at using him in a Swiss Army knife role , where he would line up at multiple positions on the field.

There are several NFL players who fit that mold, and they tend to be stars. The Baltimore Ravens use safety Kyle Hamilton at his natural position, cornerback, and linebacker, while the Philadelphia Eagles use Cooper DeJean at safety and nickel back. Tracy has a long way to go to reach the level of those two All-Pro defensive backs, but that sounds like the role Penn State envisions for him.

Keep an eye on where Tracy lines up on each play to see just how varied his positioning is.

The new Nittany Lions coach is about to get his first professional experience in the Big Ten. There isn't too much pressure for Campbell since his team will be facing a Marshall team that has almost no experience against Big Ten opponents. The former Iowa State man might not be fully comfortable in his new conference yet, so luckily, he was given an easier game to begin the season.

Over the next 12 weeks, Campbell is sure to adopt some strategies and make decisions that he never had to in the Big 12. This season will be one big adjustment for him, and Week 1 will be the perfect preview into how he handles it.

Injuries played a large factor in the 2025 season for Penn State, with linebacker Tony Rojas and defensive end Max Granville both being ruled out for the year at different points. Now, both are healthy and should be on the grass for Week 1 barring any last-minute setbacks.

Rojas looked poised to break out last season before tearing his ACL and will try to get back to that level as quickly as possible. As for Granville, he hasn't played a live snap of football in nearly two years, so all he needs to do is show positive signs of development from his freshman year.

It's been a long time since we've seen him, but now he's being depended on to be a major player on the defensive line. Keep an eye on how well Rojas and Granville respond to their injuries, but pay especially close attention to the latter this season.

While the regular season might be officially starting, it wouldn't be surprising to see the coaching staff treat the game against Marshall like an NFL preseason game. Of course, they'll prepare and respect the Thundering Herd as much as any other team, but there is little incentive to come out with an intricate game plan.

The Nittany Lions should be able to win this game handily even with a vanilla offense, so Campbell and Mouser might hold back so they don't tip their hands to scarier opponents later in the year. Watch the offensive play designs closely for Week 1 and see just how complex or generic the play calling is.

articles.title: Washington basketball to host local four-star guard on official visit
articles.summary: The Washington Huskies are set to host one of the nation's top guards in the 2027 class on an official visit.
articles.body:
Danny Sprinkle and the Washington Huskies are set to host one of the nation's top prospects on an official visit on September 5 when four-star guard Jimmie Haywood returns home.

The 6-foot-3, 170-pound product of Compass Prep in Chandler, Arizona, who is ranked as the No. 128 overall prospect and No. 15 shooting guard in the 2027 class by 247Sports, began his career at Garfield High School in Seattle before moving south.

Now, as Sprinkle prioritizes local talent as he continues to rebuild the program, Haywood could emerge as a top target for the Huskies in the months leading up to signing day.

Among Sprinkle's other top targets in the 2027 class is another local product, five-star guard Jalen Davis out of Bremerton High School, and as the Huskies look to replenish the depth on their roster through the high school ranks, the pair has the potential to become building blocks for their hometown team.

During his visit, Haywood will also likely be accompanied by five-star power forward Ahmed Nur , who is slated to arrive on Sunday, September 6. Washington is also expected to host one of the top players in the 2028 class, five-star guard Jordan Mize, on Friday, September 18.

articles.title: Former Falcons RB lands on Kansas City Chiefs practice squad
articles.summary: Former Falcons RB signs with Kansas City Chiefs practice squad
articles.body:
The Atlanta Falcons have filled out the majority of their practice squad with several players who were on their 90-man training camp roster, but not everyone returned. Former Falcons running back Nathan Carter landed with the Kansas City Chiefs' practice squad on Tuesday.

Carter, an undrafted free agent out of Michigan State, signed with Atlanta following the 2025 NFL Draft. He made the team out of training camp and appeared in seven games last season. Carter rushed nine times for 60 yards for the Falcons season but played mostly on special teams.

The second-year running back has some kick-return ability as well, which should help his chances of eventually making the Chiefs' 53-man roster. Carter had a few key blunders in the 2026 preseason that likely hurt his chances of returning, but he has some promise that Andy Reid will attempt to unlock in Kansas City.

However, the Falcons only kept two running backs on their 53-man roster. And as good as Bijan Robinson is, many were confused to see the team release veteran running back Tyler Goodson at the cut deadline. Goodson more than earned the right to be the team's third running back in training camp.

The former Colt outperformed Brian Robinson Jr. in the preseason and should arguably be in the mix for the No. 2 spot behind Bijan. Atlanta kept four quarterbacks on its initial 53-man roster, which is more confusing than anything.

We'll have to wait and see what happens, though. After all, there's still nearly two weeks until Atlanta's season opener against the Pittburgh Steelers.

articles.title: Williams sisters start US Open doubles against team with Maya Joint, who beat Serena at Wimbledon
articles.summary: Serena Williams is getting back on the court against Maya Joint — this time with sister Venus by her side.  The Williams sisters were drawn Tuesday to face t...
articles.body:
NEW YORK (AP) — Serena Williams is getting back on the court against Maya Joint — this time with sister Venus by her side.

The Williams sisters were drawn Tuesday to face the team of Hao-Ching Chan and Joint, who beat Serena at Wimbledon this summer, in their opening women's doubles match at the U.S. Open.

Serena Williams, 44, returned this year after four years out of action and lost to Joint, a 20-year-old from Australia, 6-3, 6-7 (6), 6-3. She injured her knee in the match and had to pull out of her planned doubles match at the All England Club with Venus, 46.

But they are set to compete at the U.S. Open, where the Williams sisters won the title in 1999 and 2009 and are 27-7 in their nine appearances. They last played in 2022, losing in the first round in what was expected to be Serena's final match in Flushing Meadows.

Joint and Chan are the No. 14-seeded team.

The first round of the women's doubles tournament begins Thursday.

articles.title: Lettenbichler Wins 2026 Red Bull Tennessee Knockout
articles.summary: The track was intense and the temps only added to the brutality.
articles.body:
Photos by Christian Pondella, Red Bull Content Pool

The track was intense and the temps only added to the brutality.

Manuel Lettenbichler Wins 2026 TKO Ahead of Hart and Bolt

Mani Lettenbichler won the sixteenth annual Red Bull Tennessee Knockout on his Red Bull KTM. It was the German rider's fourth TKO win at the Trials Training Center in Sequatchie, Tennessee and his third in a row. FMF KTM's Trystan Hart finished second. It was the Canadian's third consecutive runner-up finish at the TKO to go along with three wins in prior years. The UK's Billy Bolt rounded out the podium on his Husqvarna.

A total of 535 entries kicked off three days of racing on Friday with five youth and peewee classes taking on a special course in the morning. That was followed by the amateur hot laps to set the starting order for two rounds of Saturday racing followed by four rounds of pro-class racing that started on Saturday afternoon and concluded on Sunday afternoon.

The pro class racing started on Saturday afternoon with the hot-laps and Lettenbichler set the fastest time of 6:10.528. Sweden's Eddie Karlsson was closest with a 6:42.455 lap on his Stark. Hart was third with a 6:44.756 lap, and Bolt was fourth with a 6:56.682. Husqvarna's Ryder LeBlond finished fifth in 6:56.719. Toby Martyn, Cody Webb, Jonny Walker, Matthew Green and Kawelo Huddy rounded out the top ten respectively.

Trystan Hart held off a strong pack of riders to finish second at the 2026 TKO. The Canadian made a few costly mistakes during the main event.

The top sixty-six riders started the first of three knockout rounds of racing on Sunday morning on the 14-mile "long course" and the top 30 earned a trip to the TKO Knockout race two. Lettenbichler topped the time sheets again with a time of 1:01:24. Hart was just 34 seconds slower and Karlsson continued to show good form to finish just 59 seconds behind Lettenbichler. Walker was impressive on his Triumph 450 four-stroke with a time just 1:33 from the top spot and the fourth fastest time. Bolt was 3:23 behind in fifth. South African Matthew Stevens was sixth followed by Martyn, Webb, Hawaii's Kamakana Waiwaiole-Kahalepuna and fellow Hawaiian, Kawelo Huddy rounded out the top ten.

The next round changes format: a total of 31 riders (the top thirty plus one rider who earned a spot via an LCQ Straight Rhythm Duel win) are split into four groups of six and one group of seven including the LCQ winner and ride another lap on the long course with some additional hard sections added. Only the top four riders in each group qualify for the main event. Lettenbichler won group one followed by Stevens, Beta-IRC's Branden Petrie and James Flynn. Hart won group two followed by Martyn, Braxton Hintze and Riley Bender. Karlsson won group three followed by Webb, Ryder Guest and Green. Waiwaiole-Kahalepuna won group four followed by LeBlond, Walker and Makana Barger, who qualified in via the Saturday amateur racing. Bolt won group five ahead of Huddy, Niko Piazza and Coran Calvert.

Husqvarna's Billy Bolt put in a late race charge to try to take second but ultimately had to settle for third. This was still a good result in his second race back from an arm injury. Photo by Christian Pondella, Red Bull Content Pool.

The top twenty riders moved on to the main event on the short course for a multi-lap race of 45 minutes plus one lap. Hart launched into the lead at the start and led the riders into rocky creek bed, but Lettenbichler quickly took over the top spot leading into the Red Bull Ravine, which included a new obstacle called Bad Behavior followed by a technical downhill, some massive boulder sections and three technical hill climbs.

Lettenbichler led for all eight laps and finished with a total time of 59:55.957. The battle for second was intense with Karlsson pressuring Hart during the early laps before a derailed chain dropped him outside the top five. Hart took a tumble that allowed Lettenbichler to open a gap, and a crash in Bad Behavior later cost Hart the position to Bolt. Hart fought his way back to second, but Bolt kept the pressure on to the finish. Hart ended up finishing nearly three minutes behind Lettenbichler and just six seconds ahead of Bolt, who rounded out the podium.

Karlsson fought back from his derailed chain to take fourth position, just over four minutes behind Bolt. Walker crashed on the first straight but managed to work his way back up to fourth position before a small crash on the last lap dropped him back to fifth.

Cody Webb was the top American finisher in sixth position. The Yamaha YZ250X rider was in contention for the top five for most of the race.

Webb finished sixth on his Yamaha. He held fourth position early in the race before Karlsson and Walker found a way by. Martyn, the former British and US Trials champion, finished seventh on a Stark. Nineteen-year-old Stevens finished eighth on a KTM. LeBlond finished ninth on his Husqvarna and Huddy rounded out the top ten on a KTM.

2026 Red Bull Tennessee Knockout Main Event Results

The Women's pro class competed along with the top amateurs on Saturday with two rounds of racing. Rachel Gutish took the win on her Rieju and finished twenty-seventh overall. Katie Hall-Leah finished second riding a TM. Nikki Russell rounded out the podium on a GasGas.

In addition to the pro racing, the Red Bull Tennessee Knockout included several amateur classes. Saturday included two rounds of amateur racing. Hawaii's Boogie Rivera was the overall winner in both races riding a Bullet Proof Designs-backed KTM. Fellow Hawaiian Makana Barger finished second in both races on a KTM and Ayden Marinchek rounded out the top three riding a KTM. All three of those riders were competing in the A class. The top thirty riders also earned the opportunity to compete with the thirty-three pro riders, which kicked off their racing on Saturday afternoon followed by three rounds of racing on Sunday.

Other Saturday class winners among nearly 500 amateur participants included Robert Cornwell in A Vet 30+, Drew Kirby in A Senior 40+, Shawn Tescher in A Super Senior 50+, Karsen Fulton in Amateur B, Adam McCluskey in 4-Stroke Sportsman, Phillip Arnold in Schoolboy B 12-17, Benson Hickman in Youth SM-BW 12-15 and Alexis Burback in Women's Amateur.

In the eMoto Sportsman class, Australian Adam Giles took the win riding an RFN with a total time of 1:17:00. Brett Baldwin finished just six seconds behind riding a Bonnell and Isaac Johnston rounded out the podium on a Zero, just over two minutes behind.

articles.title: Who Won Last Year’s NASCAR Cup Series Southern 500 at Darlington?
articles.summary: Chase Briscoe enters as the defending winner of the Southern 500 at Darlington. Briscoe has won the last two Southern 500s.
articles.body:
Chase Briscoe aims for his third consecutive win in the Cook Out Southern 500 at Darlington Raceway this Sunday night. One year ago, the driver of the No. 19 put on a clinic in the NASCAR Cup Series Crown Jewel race, pacing the field for 309 of 367 laps around "The Track Too Tough to Tame."

This Sunday's Cook Out Southern 500 is the Chase opener, which gives Briscoe a major opportunity to climb the standings. The Joe Gibbs Racing driver is seeded fifth in the Chase standings, 45 points behind leader Denny Hamlin.

Briscoe secured dominant Darlington victory last year

In the waning laps of last year's Cook Out Southern 500, it looked as though Briscoe was on his way to a dominant. Then came a challenge for the lead.

Tyler Reddick, who was seeking his first win of the 2025 season, was breathing down the back bumper of Briscoe's No. 19 Toyota. In the end, Briscoe came out on top to claim his second straight Southern 500 victory.

Reddick finished second, followed by Erik Jones in third, John Hunter Nemechek in fourth and A.J. Allmendinger rounded out the top five.

One year prior to Briscoe's dominant 2025 run, he was in a similar position in the 2024 Southern 500. In what was the final race before the NASCAR playoffs, Briscoe, who was driving the No. 14 Stewart-Haas Racing Ford at the time, needed a win to make the cut.

Much like in 2025, Briscoe had some competition. Kyle Busch, who also needed a victory to advance in the playoffs, was stalking Briscoe in the closing laps behind the wheel of his No. 8 Richard Childress Racing Chevrolet.

Ultimately, Briscoe would prevail in what was his second career Cup victory, while Busch was forced to settle for second. The win was also the final for Stewart-Haas Racing, a team co-owned by three-time Cup Series champion Tony Stewart that ceased operations after the 2024 season.

Can Briscoe win three straight Southern 500s?

Winning at "The Track Too Tough to Tame" once is difficult enough, let alone winning at the prestigious track two times in a row.

This Sunday in Darlington, South Carolina, Briscoe will look to etch his name in the NASCAR history books. The Indiana native is seeking to win three straight of one of NASCAR's most prolific races, the Southern 500. Briscoe would be the first driver to win three straight Southern 500s since Jeff Gordon won four straight from 1995-1998.

The question is, can Briscoe do it? If last year's race is any indicator, Briscoe has to be an odds-on favorite. Yet, he might have to battle the same driver he did one year ago.

Earlier this year, Tyler Reddick claimed a win at Darlington Raceway in the Goodyear 400, his fourth of five wins in 2026. Aiming to get out of a mid-season slump, Reddick could be one for Briscoe to contender with this Sunday night.

articles.title: Orioles vs. Rockies discussion
articles.summary: After a thrilling win in the series opener, the Orioles will try to climb above.500 for the first time since April 14.
articles.body:
By gum, they've done it. The Orioles are a .500 team again. Now why don't we see how much farther this ride can take us?

The O's got back to the even-water mark last night in the most thrilling way possible, on Colton Cowser's unbelievable, gravity-defying, home run robbery that turned a certain walkoff loss into one of the most amazing wins of the season. If you were asleep when the scene played out past midnight on the East Coast, I'm sure you've seen the highlight by now. But you can never watch it too many times, so enjoy:

If the Orioles go on to make the postseason, that catch might become one of the most iconic in O's history. It still might, even if the Orioles don't make it. The Birds enter tonight just a half game behind Cleveland for the third wild card spot. If the Orioles win and the Guardians lose to the Blue Jays, the Birds will be alone in a postseason spot.

The cynical part of me thinks that tonight has all the ingredients of a huge Orioles letdown. Their vibes are sky high after last night's thrilling finish, and they're facing a starter (Gabriel Hughes) who is 0-6 with a 6.61 ERA and a Rockies team that has suffered a franchise-worst 10 straight home losses. On paper it's a game the Orioles should easily win, which always seems to be exactly when they lose. It feels like a reverse jinx.

But maybe the Orioles really are finding their groove, and they'll find a way to grind out a victory tonight just as they did in last night's opener and in all three games in Sacramento. With September call-up season upon us, they've just added some reinforcements to the roster. Luis Robert Jr., whom they claimed on waivers yesterday, has been activated, with Christian Franklin going on the IL. And Heston Kjerstad, who's been hitting well at Triple-A Norfolk for months now, is finally getting his first call-up of the season. Also joining the club is lefty prospect Luis De León, who was just converted to relief. He gives the O's another southpaw bullpen option.

For tonight, neither Robert nor Kjerstad is in the starting lineup. Neither is Coby Mayo. Pete Alonso, after returning to first base last night, is back to DHing, with Samuel Basallo spelling him at first. That means Carlos Narváez, who is 4-for-51 as an Oriole, is the catcher. Maybe facing the struggling Hughes will finally get his bat going for a night, but I'm not holding my breath.

Reaching .500 was one milestone. Now can the Orioles climb their way over? We'll find out tonight.
